question.leadin: Answer some questions about mink in history.
question.text: This president claimed that his wife, Pat, "doesn't have a mink coat" in his "Checkers" speech. This man was later forced to resign over the Watergate scandal, despite declaring "I am not a crook".
question.clue: A ruling in which this man was the respondent cited Accardi v. Shaughnessy to assert the power of the Attorney General and notes that "in camera inspection" is not a substantial diminishment of communications.

swap.leadin: Name these American generals from World War II.
swap.text: The U.S. Army's chief of staff during the war was this man, who served as Harry Truman's Secretary of State and earned a Nobel Peace Prize for his "European Recovery" plan to repair the war's damage.
swap.clue: At Dettingen, a monarch of this name became the last English king to lead troops into battle.

question.text: The Catcher in the Rye was also found in this man's possession after he assassinated John F. Kennedy.
question.clue: This man's wife Marina photographed him in the backyard holding Marxist newspapers and a rifle.

swap.text: This commander of the Apollo 11 mission, the first man to set foot on the moon, passed away in August 2012.
swap.clue: JFK's wish for a man on the moon was fulfilled when this astronaut made "one giant leap for mankind," becoming the first American on the moon.

question.leadin: This man called his own energy bill the "moral equivalent of war", which critics nicknamed MEOW.
question.text: Name this President, who blamed everything on the public's "crisis of spirit" in the Malaise speech. His failed Operation Eagle Claw led to the formation of the JSOC and the resignation of Cyrus Vance.
question.clue: This President lost his reelection bid in a race that featured Independent candidate John B. Anderson.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Senator Millard E. Tydings, a University of Maryland alumnus and building dedicatee.
swap.text: As the chair of his namesake Tydings Committee, Tydings scrutinized the accusations of this Wisconsin senator, who claimed in a speech given in Wheeling that 205 communists had infiltrated the State Department.
swap.clue: A special episode of the television show See It Now titled "A Report on" this senator and was produced by Edward R. Murrows.

question.leadin: Name these Secretaries of State of the United States of America.
question.text: This Secretary of State under Eisenhower refused to shake Zhou Enlai's hand and was a major player in overthrowing Guatemalan President Jacobo Arbenz in Operation PBSUCCESS.
question.clue: This politician's brother oversaw the MK Ultra program as CIA director until he was forced to resign following the Bay of Pigs Invasion.

swap.text: Some have argued that Reagan should not be inducted because he surrendered names of union members to this anti-communist organization during the Second Red Scare. The Hollywood Ten testified before this organization.
swap.clue: The "Hollywood Ten" were blacklisted for refusing to testify in front of this group, whose members included Jerry Voorhis and Richard Nixon.

question.text: One of the low points of Reagan's presidency was this scandal, in which the US sold arms to Iran to support Nicaraguan anti-communist rebels.
question.clue: The main perpetrator of this event was exposed when his letters to John Poindexter were discovered.

swap.text: CQ This offshoot of the Levelers was led by William Everard and Gerrard Winstanley. For 15 points, name this post-English Civil War land reform group who engaged in their namesake symbolic activity at St. George's Hill in Surrey.
swap.clue: Led early on by William Everard, the philosophy of this group was put forth in The New Law of Righteousness, the primary text by its major leader Gerrard Winstanley.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the space race.
question.text: Gagarin's space flight was a real kick in the teeth for the USA, who had been developing a program literally called "Man in Space Soonest". This man became the first American to go to space less than a month after Gagarin's orbit.
question.clue: In May, 1961, this astronaut, who hit two golf balls while on the moon, became the first American in space.

swap.leadin: This man promoted his political views in the book Why Not the Best?
swap.text: Name this politician who gave a speech officially titled "Crisis of Confidence," in which he described an inward problem plaguing America. In the so-called "malaise speech," this man urged citizens to use carpools and public transit.
swap.clue: This politician created the Department of Energy and the Department of Education, returned the Panama Canal to Panama, and signed SALT II with Leonid Brezhnev.

question.text: This failed military operation to free the hostages made Carter look even worse. Reasons for the failure included an Iranian school bus happening upon the Desert One landing site and lots of helicopter problems.
question.clue: This operation that saw the death of 8 US servicemen after a helicopter collided with a passenger plane, which Ayatollah Khomeini declared an act of God.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Church of Scientology's espionage programs in the US.
swap.text: In this operation, the Guardian's Office conducted one of the largest infiltrations of the US government in history. This operation sought to steal government documents related to church activity.
swap.answerHtml: Operation Snow White [accept answers describing a project or program called Snow White]

question.leadin: This case ruled that a section of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 was unconstitutional.
question.text: Name this 1976 Supreme Court case that held that campaign contributions, but not expenditures, can be limited in attempts to counteract corruption.
question.clue: This 1976 Supreme Court case ruled that spending money on elections is a form of free speech, but stated that limits on campaign contributions are ok.

swap.text: Whereas the Rosenbergs were actual Soviet spies, this Wisconsin Senator gave a Lincoln Day speech in Wheeling in which he produced a list of 205 supposed Communists in the State Department
swap.clue: This Wisconsin senator claimed that agents in the federal government had harbored Communists. He was brought down from grace after accusing high-ranking officers of the Army and soon died afterwards.

question.leadin: Along with Wagner and Ellender, this man sponsored the National Housing Act of 1949.
question.text: Name this Senate Majority Leader known as "Mr. Republican," who more famously sponsored a labor relations act with Fred Hartley Jr.
question.clue: One profile in the book is of this man, nicknamed Mr. Republican, an Ohio senator who was the son of a president and who opposed the Nuremberg Trials as violating American ex post facto expectations.

swap.leadin: Chaired by a former Senator, this commission implicated Robert McFarlane, in addition to others who would later be prosecuted by Lawrence Walsh.
swap.text: Identify this commission which summarized its findings in a 1987 report..
swap.clue: Edmund Muskie and Brent Scowcroft were other members of this executive branch panel, led by a former Texas Senator, which criticized the Reagan administration in its 1986 report on Iran-Contra.

question.text: In a 1971 meeting with Richard Nixon, this Ford executive convinced the president to oppose federal regulations that would make airbags mandatory on the grounds that "safety doesn't sell." This businessman wrote a best-selling autobiography in 1984 while he was CEO of Chrysler.
question.clue: This CEO of Chrysler and author of a bestselling 1984 autobiography negotiated the concessions with UAW president Doug Fraser. He had previously overseen the development of the Mustang and Pinto during his time at Ford.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about late 20th-century scandals.
swap.text: Nicknamed the "Junk Bond King," this Wall Street trader headed the high-yield bond department at Drexel Burnham Lambert until he was sold out by Ivan Boesky.
swap.clue: The LBO mania rocketed using the high-yield bonds known as "junk bonds" created by this executive at Drexel Burnham Lambert. Ivan Boesky's testimony helped lead to this financier's 1988 securities fraud conviction.
